scope: Fixed-pool physical hypothesis compression with standard farthest-first traversal. New constructed material/history pairs; no new optimizer, posterior calibration or 3D claim.
protocol: Freeze this configuration and code hashes before running. Do not tune on these outcomes.

Every pool gets exactly 49 observation callbacks and an allowance of 49 x 3 design-action trajectories. Duplicate DIRECT calls are charged. All compression rules in a pool receive the same candidates, observations and design forecasts.

Save the complete observation-only parameter/state pool and acceptance set before reading design plans. Design-aware compression changes only the rollout subset, never observational acceptance or the stored full state packet.
Design responses use simulated candidates only at 0.16, 0.29 and 0.43m/s. Compression must not read held-out impacts, targets, true parameters, pair labels or the parent experiment config.

Compare full accepted pool (reference, not an eight-state competitor), eight lowest-loss, eight parameter-diverse, eight response-diverse and three random-eight seeds. Every eight-state rule includes the same best-observation candidate.

Response features use RMS-normalized gaps at fixed 5mm scale and final separation bits at equal action normalization. Farthest-first traversal is existing k-center methodology; no algorithm novelty claim.
Primary comparison is response8 versus parameter8 and residual8 within uniform49. DIRECT and three fixed random pools are robustness controls, not independent physical trials.

Evaluate new impacts only after compression is sealed. Nearest-candidate error is an evaluation-only set diagnostic, not a deployed point forecast. Report envelope width, missing distance, coverage and failure/survival ambiguity together.
The new pairs are a held-out constructed fixture, not broad generalization. Strong observed probes can add damage. Active probe selection is not implemented in this experiment.
